comments.body:
Implemented on branch `impl-d52f`, commit `8c63584fd868ac763d9caca25fe992dabae5053a`.

## AC evidence

**AC1 — no `_heldout` path remains.** `git ls-files | grep -c '_heldout'` reads **0** on the post-change tree (it read 6 before). The expression filters *paths*, so the 57 `_heldout_` strings inside the tracked `.test_durations` and the occurrences in `src/rebar/reconciler/` and `docs/` are out of its scope by construction.

**AC2 — five renames, per-module counts preserved exactly.** Measured by collecting each module before and after:

| from | to | tests |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/interfaces/facades/test_attestation_parity_heldout_2e16.py` | `test_attestation_parity.py` | 8 |
| `tests/unit/metrics/test_dead_values_heldout_7504.py` | `test_dead_values.py` | 4 |
| `tests/unit/test_reviewed_tree_binding_heldout_da31.py` | `test_reviewed_tree_binding.py` | 9 |
| `tests/unit/test_snapshot_contract_heldout_8537.py` | **`test_snapshot_schema_contract.py`** (deviation, below) | 9 |
| `tests/unit/reconciler/mutate/test_update_priority_heldout_c9c6.py` | `test_update_priority.py` | 5 |

**AC3 — the merge.** The 10 tests from `test_code_review_provenance_heldout_2d1c.py` now live in `tests/unit/test_code_review_provenance.py`, which goes from 3 tests to **13**. There were zero test-name collisions between the two modules, and zero helper-name collisions (`_git`/`_stub_gate_run`/`repo_with_origin`/`_DIFF` against `_enable`/`_verdict`/`PROVENANCE`). The source module is deleted. Two function-local `from rebar.llm.workflow import gate_dispatch` imports were dropped because the merge target already imports that symbol at module level; the merged tests now also inherit the target's `pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit`, which does not change their selection since they already sat under `tests/unit/`.

**AC4 — whole-suite collection unchanged.** 20673 before, **20673** after. Exactly equal: no test was lost or silently duplicated.

**AC5 — detection expression.** 6 on the pre-change tree, 0 after.

Targeted run of all six affected modules: **61 passed**. `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy src/rebar scripts`, the complexity ratchet (`active=27 new=0 increased=0 stale=22`) and the mechanism ratchet all pass via the pre-commit hook.

## Documented deviation from the plan

The plan named `tests/unit/test_snapshot_contract.py` as the rename target. That basename is **already taken** by `tests/integration/reconciler/jira_contract/test_snapshot_contract.py`. Neither `tests/unit/` nor `tests/integration/reconciler/jira_contract/` is a package — only 13 `tests/**/__init__.py` exist and neither directory has one — and `pyproject.toml` configures no pytest `importmode`, so collection runs in the default `prepend` mode. Under `prepend`, two same-basename modules in two non-package directories abort collection with an import-file-mismatch error. The plan's literal target would have broken the suite outright.

`test_snapshot_schema_contract.py` is also the more accurate name: the module validates the snapshot JSON schema's accept/reject behaviour, which is a different subject from the integration contract test it would have collided with. Verified 0 remaining basename collisions across the tree after the rename.

## Noted, not acted on

`.test_durations` is tracked and holds 57 now-stale `_heldout_` test ids. Nothing polices its freshness — its only three references (`scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py:54`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_bridge_vocabulary_stale.py:32`, `tests/unit/test_check_criteria_vocabulary.py:171`) are all *exclusion*-list entries. Stale ids there degrade pytest-split's balancing slightly on the next split run and regenerate themselves; they fail nothing. Left alone as out of scope.

`make verify` is queued behind the verify currently running in another worktree.

## Defect

Epic `6ed2-24e5-6985-4faa` ("Merge held-out twin test modules after the code epics land") closed on
the strength of an acceptance criterion that measured the wrong set. Its AC1 glob was:

    git ls-files 'tests/**/test_*_heldout.py'

which returns **0 rows** at `origin/main`. The epic was therefore reported complete.

Six held-out modules are still in the tree. They are invisible to that glob because they end in
`_heldout_<4-hex-quad>.py`, not `_heldout.py`:

| LOC | tests | module | disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 137 | 8 | `tests/interfaces/facades/test_attestation_parity_heldout_2e16.py` | unpaired → rename |
| 75 | 4 | `tests/unit/metrics/test_dead_values_heldout_7504.py` | unpaired → rename |
| 122 | 9 | `tests/unit/test_reviewed_tree_binding_heldout_da31.py` | unpaired → rename |
| 145 | 9 | `tests/unit/test_snapshot_contract_heldout_8537.py` | unpaired → rename |
| 116 | 5 | `tests/unit/reconciler/mutate/test_update_priority_heldout_c9c6.py` | unpaired → rename |
| 176 | 10 | `tests/unit/test_code_review_provenance_heldout_2d1c.py` | **paired** → merge into `test_code_review_provenance.py` |

45 test functions across 6 modules. Measured at `origin/main` from worktree
`.rebar/worktrees/impl-e095` via `git ls-files --with-tree=origin/main | grep _heldout`,
a per-module `git cat-file -e origin/main:<sibling>` existence check, and
`git log --follow --name-status -M` for true creation dates.

**All six were created 2026-08-06.** The `_heldout_c9c6` module appears at 2026-10-20 under a plain
`--diff-filter=A` query, but `--follow -M` resolves that to `R100` — a pure rename from the
`rebar_reconciler` → `reconciler` package move. Its real add is `8beadd32b4c`, 2026-08-06. Nothing
has created a module under this convention in the 2.5 months since. This is pure residue, not an
active vector.

**This is not a 771-LOC deletion.** Five of the six are unpaired, so their disposition is the
rename `b721-6c6d-504e-45da` applied to the other 76 — drop the suffix, keep the tests. Only the
paired module's 10 tests fold into an existing sibling. The value here is removing the last
residue of a retired convention and fixing the oracle that hid it, not LOC.

## Why this matters beyond the residue

This is a **fail-open oracle applied to an acceptance criterion** — the same antipattern the
`tests` code-review criterion flags in test code (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md`),
occurring in an AC, where no criterion looks for it. The AC's glob was narrower than the
convention it policed, so it passed by failing to see its subject. An AC that greps for a naming
convention inherits every gap in that convention's spelling, and nothing in the close gate
compares an AC's detection expression against the population it claims to cover.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `git ls-files | grep -c '_heldout'` returns `0` at the change's HEAD.
- [ ] AC2 — The 5 unpaired modules are renamed to drop the `_heldout_<quad>` suffix, keeping every
      test function. `grep -c '^def test_'` per module is unchanged across the rename (8, 4, 9, 9,
      5 respectively), recorded in a comment before the change lands.
- [ ] AC3 — The 10 test functions in `test_code_review_provenance_heldout_2d1c.py` are merged into
      `tests/unit/test_code_review_provenance.py`, whose `grep -c '^def test_'` increases by
      exactly 10.
- [ ] AC4 — No test function is deleted. Total collected test count at the change's HEAD is
      greater than or equal to the count at its merge base, both recorded from
      `pytest --collect-only -q | tail -1`.
- [ ] AC5 — The detection expression this ticket's AC1 uses matches the `_heldout_<quad>` form,
      demonstrated by running it against the pre-change tree and observing `6`.
- [ ] AC6 — `make verify` is green at the change's HEAD.

## Explicitly out of scope

Adding a gate that would have caught the narrow AC. The generalizable defect — an AC whose
detection expression is narrower than its subject population — is worth a criterion, but it is a
separate design question and does not belong in a residue cleanup.
compiled_state.title: 6ed2's AC1 glob cannot see the _heldout_<quad> naming form, so 6 held-out modules (771 LOC) survived the merge epic
